q13.question: When is my tuition bill due this fall?
q13.luna_run1: For Fall 2026, your tuition due date depends on when you first registered: March 19–July 19: August 3; July 20–August 7: August 14; August 8–27: August 27; August 28 or later: immediately upon registration. [1]

q14.question: When will my financial aid refund be issued this fall?
q14.luna_run1: For Fall 2026, the main refund date for the remaining 75% of the Federal Pell Grant and other aid programs, including Federal Direct Loans, was October 5, 2026. After that date, refunds are issued weekly as students become eligible. [1] The Fall 2026 schedule also lists refund dates through November 27, 2026. [2]

q54.question: What happens if I fail a math course?
q54.luna_run1: If you fail a math course, the source says to retake it the very next semester; if you fail in spring, it says you may consider retaking it over the summer. [1] When you pass, a grade of C or higher replaces the failing grade in GPA calculations, but the failed course remains on your transcript. [1] On the degree audit, the highest grade from a repeated course counts toward degree requirements; after the second attempt, the lower grade is listed as insufficient and does not count toward credits or requirements. [3] A delay in taking math courses could delay graduation, and some STEM majors require at least a C in math to progress. [2]

q59.question: What happens if I don't pay my tuition bill?
q59.luna_run1:
If you don’t pay tuition or other obligations, you may lose access to your records and be prevented from registering in the future. Your account may be sent to the College’s collection agency, and you may be responsible for collection costs, including agency fees, attorney fees, and court costs. Nonpayment or a default judgment may also be reported to credit bureaus and appear on your credit report. [1]

For **Fall 2026**, unpaid tuition after enrollment can result in a hold that prevents adding or swapping courses; failure to pay by your due date could result in cancellation of course enrollment. [2] Delinquent students must also pay a **$15 non-payment service fee** to regain privileges of good fiscal standing, in addition to outstanding bills. [3]
